_note: Treatment guides for Sehatsandhi International (4 Nov 2026). General information written by the Sehatsandhi team, not medical advice; the treating doctor's instructions come first. Loaded by migration 0322 into intl_procedures.guide and intl_machines.

new_procedures.name: Chemotherapy (per cycle)
new_procedures.summary: Cancer medicines given by drip or tablets in planned cycles, usually in a day-care unit, under a medical oncologist.
new_procedures.reports: Biopsy and histopathology report, PET-CT or CT scans, blood counts, kidney and liver tests, treatment history and any previous chemotherapy details

new_procedures.name: Radiotherapy (course)
new_procedures.summary: High-energy X-rays aimed precisely at a tumour, given in short daily sessions over a few weeks, planned by a radiation oncologist.
new_procedures.reports: Biopsy report, recent MRI, CT or PET-CT, surgery notes if operated, previous radiotherapy details

new_procedures.name: MRI scan
new_procedures.summary: Detailed pictures of the brain, spine, joints and organs using a strong magnet and radio waves — no X-rays.
new_procedures.reports: The doctor's referral or question, previous scans, a list of any metal implants, pacemaker or devices in the body

new_procedures.name: CT scan
new_procedures.summary: Fast, detailed cross-section X-ray pictures of the body, often with a contrast dye.
new_procedures.reports: The doctor's referral, previous scans, kidney function test if contrast is planned, allergy history

new_procedures.name: PET-CT scan
new_procedures.summary: A whole-body scan that shows how active tissues are, mainly used to find, stage and follow up cancer.
new_procedures.reports: Biopsy report, previous scans, blood sugar readings (diabetes affects this scan), treatment history

machines.name: MRI scanner
machines.what: A large tube-shaped magnet that makes detailed pictures without X-rays. The scan is painless but loud; you lie still for 20–45 minutes.
machines.scene: A modern MRI scanner in a clean, bright hospital imaging room, white tunnel-shaped machine with a patient table, no people

machines.name: CT scanner
machines.what: A ring-shaped X-ray machine that takes cross-section pictures in a few minutes. You lie on a table that moves through the ring.
machines.scene: A modern CT scanner with its ring-shaped gantry and patient table in a clean hospital imaging room, no people

machines.name: PET-CT scanner
machines.what: A CT scanner combined with a PET camera that detects a small dose of tracer, showing which tissues are most active.
machines.scene: A PET-CT scanner with a long gantry and patient table in a calm nuclear medicine room with soft lighting, no people

machines.name: Linear accelerator (radiotherapy)
machines.what: The machine that gives radiotherapy. It rotates around you and shapes the beam to the tumour; each session takes minutes and does not hurt.
machines.scene: A modern radiotherapy linear accelerator machine with a treatment couch in a spacious, softly lit treatment room, no people

machines.name: Chemotherapy day-care unit
machines.what: Comfortable recliner chairs with infusion pumps, where chemotherapy is given by trained oncology nurses.
machines.scene: A calm, bright chemotherapy day-care room with comfortable reclining chairs, infusion stands and large windows, no people

machines.name: Cath lab
machines.what: A special X-ray room where cardiologists look inside heart arteries and place stents through a thin tube in the wrist or groin.
machines.scene: A modern cardiac catheterisation lab with a C-shaped X-ray arm, monitors and a patient table, clean and empty

machines.name: Heart-lung machine
machines.what: Takes over the work of the heart and lungs during open-heart surgery such as bypass or valve replacement, run by a perfusionist.
machines.scene: A heart-lung bypass machine with pumps and tubing beside an empty operating table in a modern cardiac operation theatre, no people

machines.name: Modular operation theatre
machines.what: A sealed operating room with filtered air flowing down over the table, which lowers infection risk for joint and implant surgery.
machines.scene: An empty modern modular operation theatre with stainless steel walls, overhead surgical lights and a laminar airflow ceiling

machines.name: C-arm X-ray
machines.what: A mobile X-ray unit used during joint and spine surgery so the surgeon can check implant position in real time.
machines.scene: A mobile C-arm X-ray machine standing in an empty modern operation theatre

machines.name: Laparoscopy (keyhole surgery) tower
machines.what: A camera and screen system for keyhole surgery through small cuts — less pain and a quicker recovery than open surgery.
machines.scene: A laparoscopic surgery tower with a high-definition monitor and camera unit beside an empty operating table

machines.name: Phaco machine and operating microscope
machines.what: Used in cataract surgery: the cloudy lens is broken up with ultrasound and removed through a tiny cut, viewed under a microscope.
machines.scene: An ophthalmic operating microscope and a phacoemulsification machine in a clean, empty eye operation theatre

machines.name: Excimer laser (LASIK)
machines.what: A precise laser that reshapes the front of the eye to correct vision; the treatment itself takes seconds per eye.
machines.scene: A modern refractive laser eye surgery machine with a patient bed in a clean, bright clinic room, no people

machines.name: Dental CBCT scanner
machines.what: A 3D dental X-ray that shows the jaw bone, so implants can be planned precisely.
machines.scene: A modern dental cone beam CT scanner standing in a clean, bright dental clinic room, no people

machines.name: IVF laboratory
machines.what: A controlled lab with incubators and microscopes where eggs are fertilised and embryos grow before transfer.
machines.scene: A clean IVF embryology laboratory with incubators, an inverted microscope and a laminar flow workstation, soft lighting, no people

machines.name: Lithotripsy and urology laser
machines.what: Breaks kidney stones into small pieces with shock waves or a laser, often without any cut.
machines.scene: A modern lithotripsy machine with a patient table in a clean urology procedure room, no people

machines.name: Ultrasound and Doppler
machines.what: Uses sound waves to see organs, blood flow and veins — painless and without radiation.
machines.scene: A modern ultrasound machine with a screen and probe beside an examination bed in a bright clinic room, no people

cataract.about: The surgeon makes a tiny cut, breaks up the cloudy lens with ultrasound and places a clear artificial lens. It usually takes under half an hour under numbing drops.
before: A full eye check and lens measurement (biometry)
Control blood sugar and blood pressure
Tell the doctor about blood thinners and eye drops you use
after: Vision clears over a few days to weeks
Use the prescribed drops exactly as advised
Most people return to daily activities within days; glasses may be updated after a few weeks
dos: Wear the eye shield at night for the first week
donts: Do not rub or press the eye
Avoid swimming and dusty places for 2 weeks
Avoid eye make-up for a few weeks
Do not lift heavy weights in the first week

lasik.about: A laser reshapes the front surface of the eye (cornea) to reduce dependence on glasses. Not every eye is suitable; tests decide.
before: Stop soft contact lenses about a week before (hard lenses longer) for accurate tests
No eye make-up on the day
after: Mild grittiness for a day or two
Dry eyes are common for a few weeks
dos: Wear eye shields while sleeping for a few nights
donts: Do not rub your eyes
No swimming for 2 weeks
Avoid screens for long stretches in the first days

glaucoma.about: Surgery creates a new drainage path (or places a small device) to lower eye pressure when drops or laser are not enough. It aims to protect remaining vision; lost vision does not come back.
before: Eye pressure, visual field and OCT tests
Control blood sugar and blood pressure
after: Frequent check-ups in the first weeks
Vision may be blurred for a few weeks
donts: Do not bend low or lift heavy weights early on
Do not rub the eye
Do not stop drops without advice

dental_implant.about: A titanium post is placed in the jaw bone and, after it bonds, holds a crown. Some cases need bone grafting or two visits.
before: Tell the dentist about smoking, diabetes and medicines
after: Mild swelling for a few days
Soft food for a week or two
The final crown is fitted once the implant settles
donts: Do not smoke — it slows healing
Avoid hard and very hot food early on
Do not chew on the implant side before advised

dental_smile.about: Damaged teeth are saved with root canal treatment and protected with crowns, or gaps filled with bridges.
before: Tell the dentist about sensitivity and medicines
after: Mild tenderness for a few days
Temporary crowns are replaced with permanent ones
dos: Use a night guard if you grind your teeth
donts: Do not bite hard objects on new crowns
Avoid sticky sweets on temporary crowns

hernia.about: The weak spot in the abdominal wall is repaired, usually with a mesh, often by keyhole surgery.
before: Stop blood thinners only if your doctor says so
dos: Eat fibre and drink water to avoid straining
donts: No heavy lifting for 4–6 weeks
Do not strain on the toilet
Do not drive while on strong pain medicines

gallbladder.about: The gallbladder is removed through small cuts (laparoscopic cholecystectomy). People live normally without it.
after: Home in a day or two
Shoulder-tip pain from the gas settles in days
donts: Avoid heavy, oily food for a few weeks
No heavy lifting for 2–4 weeks

piles.about: Piles, fissures or fistulas are treated with laser or surgery, depending on type and grade.
after: Most people return to work within a week
dos: High-fibre diet and plenty of water
donts: Do not strain or sit long on the toilet
Avoid spicy food early on
Do not lift heavy weights for 2 weeks

kidney_stone.about: Stones are broken with shock waves (ESWL) or a laser through a thin scope, without cuts; large stones may need keyhole surgery.
before: Urine test to rule out infection
after: Stone fragments pass in urine over days
A small tube (stent) may stay for a few weeks
Some burning on passing urine at first
dos: Ask about diet to prevent new stones
donts: Do not ignore fever or severe pain — get help
Do not cut fluids

varicose.about: Swollen leg veins are closed from inside with laser or radio-frequency heat, through a needle-hole.
donts: Avoid standing still for long
No hot baths or saunas for a few weeks

ent_sinus.about: Endoscopic sinus surgery, septoplasty or tonsil removal is done through the nose or mouth, with no outside cut.
after: Blocked nose for a week or two
Throat pain after tonsil removal for 1–2 weeks
dos: Soft, cool food after tonsil surgery
donts: Do not blow the nose hard
Avoid flying for the advised period
No heavy exercise for 2 weeks

health_checkup.about: A planned set of blood tests, scans and doctor consultations, usually in one or two days, with reports explained.
before: Fast overnight if blood sugar and cholesterol tests are planned
Bring previous reports and medicine list
after: Reports explained the same or next day
A doctor advises on any follow-up
dos: Share reports with your own doctor
donts: Do not stop medicines before tests unless told

knee_replacement.about: The worn surfaces of the knee are replaced with metal and plastic parts. Most people stand the next day with support.
before: Prepare home: clear rugs, firm chair
after: Walker or stick for a few weeks
dos: Keep the wound dry and clean
donts: Do not kneel or squat early on
No long sitting with the knee bent
Do not skip blood-thinner doses if prescribed

hip_replacement.about: The damaged hip joint is replaced with an implant. Walking starts within a day or two.
before: Arrange a raised toilet seat and firm chair
after: Normal walking in weeks to months
donts: Do not cross your legs
Do not bend the hip beyond 90 degrees early on
Avoid low chairs

shoulder_arthroscopy.about: A camera and small tools repair torn tissue inside the joint through small cuts.
after: Sling or brace for some weeks
donts: Do not lift with the operated arm early on
Do not remove the sling before advised

spine_disc.about: The part of a disc pressing on a nerve is removed, often through a small cut with a microscope or endoscope.
after: Walking the same or next day
Back exercises after a few weeks
donts: Do not bend and twist
No heavy lifting for 6 weeks
Avoid long car journeys early on

spine_fusion.about: Two or more spinal bones are joined with screws, rods and bone graft to stop painful movement or correct shape.
before: Stop smoking — it affects bone healing
dos: Follow the brace and lifting rules
donts: Do not smoke
No bending, lifting or twisting early on
Do not take anti-inflammatory painkillers unless prescribed

hysterectomy.about: The uterus is removed, often by keyhole surgery. Ovaries may or may not be removed — discuss with your surgeon.
before: Discuss what will be removed and why
dos: Rest, but avoid long bed rest
donts: No heavy lifting for 6 weeks
No intercourse for about 6 weeks
Do not drive until comfortable braking

ivf.about: Hormone injections stimulate the ovaries, eggs are collected and fertilised in the lab, and an embryo is placed in the uterus.
before: Hormone tests (AMH, FSH) and semen analysis
Read the legal notes on IVF in India
after: A pregnancy test about two weeks after transfer
Not every cycle succeeds — ask about your chances
donts: Do not smoke or drink alcohol
Avoid very strenuous exercise
Do not ask for sex selection — it is illegal

angioplasty.about: A narrowed heart artery is opened with a balloon through a thin tube in the wrist or groin, and a stent keeps it open.
before: Angiography report or CD, echo, ECG
after: Home in a day or two
dos: Take blood thinners without missing a dose
donts: Never stop blood thinners without your cardiologist
Do not smoke
No heavy lifting for a week

prostate.about: The part of an enlarged prostate blocking urine flow is removed through the urine passage with a scope or laser.
before: PSA test, ultrasound, urine flow test
after: A catheter for a day or two
Some blood in urine for a few weeks
donts: Do not strain or lift heavy weights for 4 weeks
Avoid cycling early on

thyroid.about: Part or all of the thyroid gland is removed through a small cut in the neck.
after: Mild neck discomfort and hoarse voice for a short time
Thyroid tablets may be needed for life
dos: Take thyroid and calcium tablets exactly as prescribed
Report tingling in fingers or lips
donts: Do not stop thyroid tablets
Avoid heavy neck strain for 2 weeks

bariatric.about: Keyhole surgery makes the stomach smaller (sleeve) or changes the food route (bypass) to support long-term weight loss.
before: Weight, blood tests, sleep study if advised
after: Liquid then soft diet for weeks
donts: Do not drink with meals
Avoid sugary drinks and alcohol
Do not skip follow-ups

heart_bypass.about: Blocked heart arteries are bypassed with blood vessels from the chest, leg or arm. The heart-lung machine may support the body during surgery.
after: ICU for a day or two, then ward
dos: Walk a little more each day
donts: No lifting over 2–3 kg or pushing with arms for 6–8 weeks
Do not smoke
Do not drive for 4–6 weeks

heart_valve.about: A damaged heart valve is repaired or replaced with a mechanical or tissue valve.
after: Mechanical valves need lifelong blood thinners with regular tests
dos: Keep INR blood tests if on warfarin
Tell every dentist you have a valve
donts: Do not miss blood-thinner doses
No heavy lifting for 6–8 weeks

brain_tumour.about: A neurosurgical team removes as much of the tumour as is safe, often with navigation and a microscope.
before: Discuss risks and plan with the surgeon
dos: Take seizure and steroid medicines as prescribed
Rest and build up activity slowly
donts: Do not drive until cleared
Do not stop medicines suddenly

cancer_surgery.about: The tumour is removed, planned together with medical and radiation oncologists. Further treatment may follow.
donts: Do not miss follow-ups
Do not take herbal remedies without telling your oncologist

chemotherapy.about: Cancer medicines are given in cycles — often every 2–3 weeks — by drip or tablets, usually without staying overnight. The plan depends on the cancer type and stage.
before: A dental check and a plan for your stay in India across cycles
after: Tiredness, nausea or low blood counts are common and managed with medicines
dos: Wash hands often and avoid crowds when counts are low
Eat small, frequent meals and drink water
donts: Do not eat raw or undercooked food
Do not take other medicines or supplements without asking
Do not skip blood tests

radiotherapy.about: A planning CT maps the tumour, then high-energy X-rays from a linear accelerator are given in short daily sessions, usually 5 days a week for a few weeks.
before: Plan to stay for the whole course
after: Tiredness and skin redness in the treated area are common
Side effects settle weeks after the course
dos: Wash treated skin gently with mild soap
donts: Do not apply creams on treated skin unless approved
Avoid sun on treated skin
Do not miss sessions

mri_scan.about: You lie still inside the scanner for 20–45 minutes. It is noisy but painless; earplugs are given. Sometimes a contrast injection is used.
before: Tell staff about pacemakers, implants, metal pieces or pregnancy
Tell staff if you feel anxious in closed spaces
after: Go back to normal activities straight away
dos: Lie still and follow breathing instructions
donts: Do not take any metal into the room

ct_scan.about: A quick X-ray scan, usually a few minutes. A contrast dye may be given by drip or drink.
before: Kidney test if contrast is planned
Tell staff about allergies, diabetes medicines (metformin) or pregnancy
Fast a few hours if asked
dos: Lie still and hold breath when asked
donts: Do not hide allergy history

pet_ct.about: A small dose of radioactive sugar is injected; after about an hour of rest, the scan takes 20–30 minutes and shows active tissue across the body.
before: Control blood sugar — tell staff if you are diabetic
Avoid heavy exercise the day before
after: Drink water to flush the tracer
Keep a distance from pregnant women and small children for some hours
dos: Rest quietly while the tracer spreads
donts: Do not eat before the scan
Do not exercise strenuously the day before

kidney_transplant.about: A kidney from a near-relative living donor is placed in the lower abdomen. Read the legal notes: foreign patients need committee approval.
before: Matching tests for donor and patient
after: Several weeks in India for close monitoring
dos: Take anti-rejection medicines on time, every day
donts: Never miss a dose
Do not take any medicine or herbal product without the transplant team

liver_transplant.about: Part of a liver from a near-relative living donor replaces a failed liver. Read the legal notes: foreign patients need committee approval.
before: Detailed tests for donor and patient
dos: Follow the transplant team's diet and medicine plan
donts: Do not drink alcohol
Do not take medicines without the transplant team

bone_marrow.about: After high-dose treatment, healthy blood stem cells are given by drip to rebuild the bone marrow. Read the legal notes.
donts: Avoid crowds and sick people
Do not skip follow-up tests

child_heart.about: Heart defects present at birth are corrected by surgery or through a catheter, by a paediatric cardiac team.
after: Regular check-ups as the child grows
donts: Do not miss follow-up echoes
